General RRCReconfiguration (sent via other RAT) RRCReconfigurationComplete"**

— and cross-referencing with [7], which describes the initiation of handover *to NR* **via other RAT**, the procedure corresponds to the completion signaling for an RRC reconfiguration received during an inter-RAT handover (e.g., from E-UTRA to NR).

Crucially, [7] states:

> "The RAN using another RAT initiates the handover to NR procedure, in accordance with the specifications applicable for the other RAT, by sending the RRCReconfiguration message via the radio access technology from which the inter-RAT handover is performed."

And [5] (Clause 5.3.5.3) specifies the UE’s behavior upon reception, including that:

> 2 > if the RRCReconfiguration includes the fullConfig:  
> 3 > perform the full configuration procedure as specified in 5.3.5.11;  
> ...  
> 1 > set the content of the RRCReconfigurationComplete message as follows:  
> ..."

Thus, while no single sentence in the context *explicitly defines the purpose*, the **only extractive text directly naming the procedure** is the clause title itself — and it is consistently paired with inter-RAT handover to NR.

Therefore, per instruction to prefer copying a text span **from the provided clauses**, and since no explicit “purpose” statement exists beyond the heading, the answer is the heading verbatim — as it is the sole authoritative label for the procedure in the context:

**General RRCReconfiguration (sent via other RAT) RRCReconfigurationComplete**

results.question: For an UTRA-FDD cell with reportType set to periodical and a single quantity not set to true, what is the sorting quantity?
results.reference: consider RSCP as the sorting quantity
results.gold_evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.5.3, Sorting of cell measurement results
results.model_answer:
For an UTRA-FDD cell with reportType set to periodical and a single quantity not set to true, the sorting quantity is **RSCP**.

From Clause 5.5.5.3:

> 2 > determine the sorting quantity according to reportQuantityUTRA-FDD for UTRA-FDD cell, as below:  
> 3 > if a single quantity is set to true:  
> 4 > consider this quantity as the sorting quantity;  
> 4 > consider RSCP as the sorting quantity.

The text does **not** condition the "consider RSCP as the sorting quantity" clause on `a single quantity is set to true`; rather, it appears as a standalone alternative under the same indentation level (item 4), following the conditional item 3. However, examining the exact structure in [5]:

> 2 > determine the sorting quantity according to reportQuantityUTRA-FDD for UTRA-FDD cell, as below:  
> 3 > if a single quantity is set to true:  
> 4 > consider this quantity as the sorting quantity;  
> 4 > consider RSCP as the sorting quantity.

This formatting (both item 4s at same level, no “else”) is ambiguous — but per 3GPP TS 38.331 v17.11.0 (and consistent interpretation in RAN2), when *no single quantity is set to true*, the default fallback for UTRA-FDD in periodical reporting is **RSCP**, as explicitly stated in the second item 4.

Thus, the extractive answer is:

**RSCP**
results.evidence: TS 38.331, Clause 5.5.2.8, Quantity configuration
